title: Petra and the Thorn
premise: Bram Crane, a royal food-taster immune to poison by slow habituation, has spent her life in the Thornvale, a valley where magic cannot enter—until a dying courier gives her a map to the palace's hidden heart and warns that the king is being consumed by the entity wearing his crown. Guided by the map and hunted by the crown's enforcers, Bram discovers her immunity is no accident: she was bred as a vessel, the last uncorrupted bloodline capable of unbinding the king. To save him she must take the crown's binding into herself, choosing love over the invisibility she always craved. In the end she shatters the thorn-crown at terrible cost, freeing the king but exiling herself from the valley forever—and finding belonging not in a place, but in the person who chooses to follow her out.
about_author: Astrid Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval herbals and poison gardens before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about quiet people caught in loud histories, from a cottage full of pressed flowers and half-finished maps.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet Bram in the Thornvale, tasting the lord's food with practiced calm while hiding how much of her life is performance—invisible, safe, magicless. A stranger collapses at the market gate, bleeding shadow instead of blood, and presses a wax-sealed map into her hands with the words 'the king is already dead.' Emotional beat: the crack in her carefully built ordinary life.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The map burns cold in her keeping; the valley's wards reject it, and Bram realizes anything touched by magic cannot stay. When crown enforcers arrive asking after a courier, her mentor lies for her and pays with his life. Grieving and cornered, Bram slips past the wardline at dawn. Emotional beat: exile chosen before courage arrives.

chapters.title: A Road of Small Poisons
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, intercut with the king's fevered dreams. On the road to the capital, Bram survives an ambush using her trained palate—identifying toxins in the air, the water, a proffered apple. She meets Wren, a disgraced court physician who recognizes the map's seal and offers passage. Emotional beat: first fragile alliance; Bram learns her skill is power, not just servitude.

chapters.title: The Court of Hungry Faces
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inside the capital, Wren shows Bram a court gone subtly wrong: nobles with thorn-scars at their collars, servants who smile too long. The queen died a year ago; no one will say how. Bram secures a place in the kitchens as a taster, close to the king's table. Emotional beat: dread dressed as ambition; the corruption is systemic, not one man's curse.

chapters.title: The King Who Tastes of Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Summoned to taste for the king himself, Bram finds Aldric young, lucid for moments at a time, and terrified—he begs her, between dishes, to let him die. The crown of black iron thorns drinks everything he loves. He recognizes the map's maker: his late queen. Emotional beat: love begins here, in pity sharpened into devotion.

chapters.title: Rootwork
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Researching the queen's papers, Wren uncovers the truth: the crown was made to protect the realm, and it protects it the way a cage protects a bird. Worse, records reveal the tasters' guild bred 'clean vessels'—Bram among them—to eventually wear or break the crown. Emotional beat: betrayal; Bram's whole identity was someone else's plan.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crown, sensing Bram's approach, takes the king fully: Aldric orders her execution with a voice like roots splitting stone. She escapes the dungeon through the poison garden with Wren's help, learning the crown fears her immunity—it cannot root in her. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; she is the flaw in its design.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In hiding beneath the city, Bram trains with Wren to withstand the crown's binding, dosing herself with extracts of the thorn-plant as she once dosed against poison—building immunity to magic itself, one agonizing dose at a time. Aldric, surfacing briefly, sends her a message of warning and something dangerously like hope. Emotional beat: sacrifice rehearsed; love declared obliquely, through a vial left where she'll find it.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram walks into the throne room during the solstice rite and lets the crown take hold of her, fighting it from inside while Wren works the queen's counter-ritual below. She reaches Aldric within the binding and offers him her hand instead of the crown's roots. Climax: together they shatter the thorn-crown; the backlash scars the palace and severs Bram from the valley's safety forever. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved by refusing the choice itself.

chapters.title: Beyond the Wardline
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, closing with Aldric's. The realm mends slowly under a king who remembers what wore him. Bram, now marked by magic and unable to re-enter the Thornvale, expects to be alone—but Aldric abdicates his isolation alongside her, walking out past the wardline at her side. They plant the crown's shattered iron in a garden where nothing grows, and something green appears anyway. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a place, but in being chosen.
